A first securing element is configured to secure the light guide in a first position, while a second securing element is configured to secure the light guide in a second position. The first and second positions are spaced apart from one another along the longitudinal extension of the light guide by a first distance.

The carrier structure includes an intermediate carrier having two opposing surfaces. A first surface of the intermediate carrier carries or supports the first and second securing elements. An opposing second surface of the intermediate carrier is configured to be applied to, or placed against, a measurement object.

The arrangement of the securing elements on the intermediate carrier is such that the distance between the securing positions defined on the intermediate carrier is greater than the distance between the corresponding secured positions along the longitudinal extension of the light guide. outputs.L4:
A clamping device for a light guide is provided for positioning and holding the light guide relative to a measurement object. The device includes a carrier structure which supports the light guide at two spaced locations. For this purpose, the carrier structure has a first securing element and a second securing element, each of which is configured to fix or clamp the light guide at a respective securing point. The two securing elements are arranged on an intermediate carrier.

The intermediate carrier has a surface facing away from the securing elements. This opposing surface is configured so that it can be applied to, placed against, or mounted on a measurement object. In this way, the intermediate carrier forms a defined interface between the light guide and the object to be measured. The measurement object may, for example, be a component whose deformation, strain, displacement, temperature, or other physical property is to be detected by means of the light guide.

The first and second securing elements are positioned on the intermediate carrier at securing positions which are spaced apart from one another by a first distance. The light guide, however, is secured by these elements at two secured positions along its length which are spaced apart by a second distance. The first distance between the securing positions on the intermediate carrier is greater than the second distance between the secured positions on the light guide. As a result of this geometric arrangement, the light guide can be guided, deflected, preloaded, tensioned, or otherwise positioned in a controlled manner when it is fixed to the securing elements.

This configuration enables the light guide to be held in a defined mechanical state. In particular, the difference between the spacing of the securing elements on the intermediate carrier and the spacing of the corresponding secured portions of the light guide can generate a predetermined tensile force, curvature, or contact condition. This can improve the reproducibility and accuracy of measurements, since the light guide is maintained in a known position relative to the measurement object.

The clamping device is therefore especially suitable for measurement applications in which a light guide, such as an optical fibre or optical waveguide, must be precisely arranged on or near a component. The device can be used, for example, in optical sensing systems in which changes in light transmission, reflection, wavelength, phase, or intensity are evaluated to determine a physical condition of the measurement object. By using the intermediate carrier and the two spaced securing elements, the light guide can be mounted reliably, repeatably, and with a defined preload, thereby improving measurement stability and reducing installation variability.

counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Disclosure — Clamping Device for a Light Guide

A clamping device (300) for securing a light guide (112) is disclosed. The clamping device (300) comprises an intermediate carrier and at least a first securing element and a second securing element arranged on or formed integrally with the intermediate carrier.

The first securing element is configured to engage the light guide (112) at a first light-guide position, and the second securing element is configured to engage the light guide (112) at a second light-guide position spaced apart from the first light-guide position. The first securing element is secured to, supported by, or connected with the intermediate carrier at a first securing position. The second securing element is secured to, supported by, or connected with the intermediate carrier at a second securing position spaced apart from the first securing position.

The intermediate carrier defines the relative arrangement of the first and second securing elements and thereby provides a controlled clamping geometry for the light guide (112). In particular, a distance between the first securing position and the second securing position is different from a distance between the first light-guide position and the second light-guide position. Preferably, the distance between the first and second securing positions is selected such that, when the light guide (112) is received by the first and second securing elements, the securing elements are elastically deflected and exert a clamping force on the light guide (112).

In one embodiment, the distance between the first and second securing positions is smaller than the distance between the first and second light-guide positions, so that the first and second securing elements are biased outwardly when engaging the light guide (112). In another embodiment, the distance between the first and second securing positions is greater than the distance between the first and second light-guide positions, so that the securing elements are biased inwardly. In either case, the difference between the securing-position spacing and the light-guide-position spacing produces a defined preload that holds the light guide (112) relative to the intermediate carrier.

The clamping device (300) thereby allows the light guide (112) to be mounted in a reproducible position while compensating for manufacturing tolerances, thermal expansion, or assembly deviations. The intermediate carrier may further be configured for attachment to a housing, support frame, optical module, or other structural component.
